Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service New York NY
223 AM EST Wed Nov 18 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
No significant changes from previous forecast.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1) Dry and warmer through the week.

2) Next chance of rain late Sunday into early next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
.KEY MESSAGE 1...
Strong surface high pressure conditions to dominate the weather over 
much of the eastern half of the country through the end of the week and 
into the beginning of the weekend. As the high slowly shifts over the 
area into the middle to end of the week, temperatures will begin to 
moderate a bit more such that by Friday, high temperatures will
rise into the upper 50s to middle 60s. 

Given the clear and dry conditions under a weak pressure gradient, low 
temperatures each night through at least Thursday will be largely 
determined by the extent of radiational cooling. By Thursday night, a 
SW direction to the flow should allow subtle moisture advection which 
will limit the extent of the falling nighttime temperatures into the 
weekend.

.KEY MESSAGE 2...

A vertically stacked coastal low appears likely to develop off
the Southeast coast this weekend. The sys is then progged to 
lift to the NE as an upr trof approaches. There remains 
significant uncertainty regarding the exact track and timing of 
the low into next week, but the potential remains for the area 
to receive 1-2 inches of rain with locally higher amounts from 
late Sunday into the beginning of next week. 

The 00Z GFS and 00Z AI-GFS remain hits for the local area,
bringing rain up the coast late Sun and persisting thru Mon. The
ECMWF remains further out to sea with limited to no impacts. 

The NBM consensus brings roughly a 30-60 percent chance of rain
to the area, and these numbers were accepted considering the
uncertainty this far out. The modeling does suggest a sharp
gradient on the wrn edge of the pcpn field. 

The modeling also indicates the potential for the low to drop
into the 980s close to the area. This would produce some gusty
winds for at least some of the cwa. Winds will be proportional 
to the depth of the low, so in this case would estimate peak 
gusts in the 30-40mph range based on the 00Z GFS/AI-GFS. There 
are some hints of a deeper low, with the ECMWF in the 960s S of 
the benchmark after traversing the Gulf Stream. A track that far
E however would have limited impacts despite the intensity. 

&&

.AVIATION /07Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
High pressure remains in the area through the TAF period with VFR 
conditions continuing.

Winds will be 5 kts or less with variable direction outside of 
the NYC terminals late tonight into the morning, while KJFK, 
KLGA, and KEWR will be from the W-WNW near 5-8 kts.

Mainly a WSW-WNW flow near 5-10 kts expected Wednesday late morning 
through Wednesday afternoon. Some terminals could have more SW flow 
by mid to late afternoon.

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

Wind direction could be off by 20-30 degrees from TAF at times 
tonight and Wednesday.

For Wednesday, the wind direction could have more of a southerly 
component than forecast during the afternoon.

.OUTLOOK FOR 06Z Thursday through Sunday... 

Late Wednesday night-Saturday: VFR.

Sunday: Chance of MVFR or lower at times with rain forecast.

Detailed information, including hourly TAF wind component forecasts, 
can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

&&

.MARINE...
High pressure will remain in control of the weather through the
week with sub-SCA conditions. Winds will mostly be from the 
NW-W at less than 15kt with seas on the ocean no higher than 2 
to 3 ft. Building seas can be expected on Sun, with a SCA 
possibly needed by Sun night.
